title: 2027-10-14 Edgewise AI embeddings + rerank discovery
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment
summary: Intro discovery for embeddings + reranking. Edgewise wants to replace an ad-hoc FAISS + Postgres pipeline with a more reliable rerank flow. Discussed workload (QPS, latency SLOs), index backends, dimensionality tradeoffs (1536 vs 768 vs 128), and hosted vs dedicated vs private options. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send detailed pricing, security pack, and run a short benchmark with 100k vectors using their sample corpus.
action_items: Ethan Li - send hosted vs dedicated vs private comparison + indicative pricing - 2027-10-18
Priya Raman - propose benchmark plan (100k vectors, 1k QPS synthetic, hybrid search) - 2027-10-20
Liam O'Connor - share sample dataset + current index stats (dimensionality, cardinality) - 2027-10-16
next_steps: Redwood to provision trial access for hosted API and a dedicated trial node
Customer to provide 100k sample vectors and baseline latency numbers
Schedule technical benchmark next week (Priya + Liam)
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-10-14 16:00 UTC | Duration 48m | Attendees: Ethan, Priya - Redwood; Liam, Sofia, Mark - Edgewise

00:00 Ethan Li: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, can you hear me okay?
00:03 Liam O'Connor: Yep yep, loud and clear. Thanks for setting this up.
00:06 Ethan Li: Cool. So objective for today is to understand your embedding/reranking flow and whether Redwood hosted or dedicated or private makes sense. Priya will jump in on perf and architecture.
00:15 Priya Raman: Hi all, quick intro — I focus on performance and infra, mainly on batching, KV cache and routing. I might call out tradeoffs between throughput and latency.
00:25 Mark Tan: Great. Quick context: we're Edgewise, we power a relevance layer for news and internal docs. Right now we run a FAISS index + a small BERT reranker on CPU. We're seeing tail latency spikes and high ops cost when traffic bursts. We're evaluating a re-architecture with vector DB + LLM-based rerank.
00:40 Sofia Hernandez: Our current index is about 1.2M vectors at 768 dims and we run nightly rebuilds. Typical QPS is 200 steady with spikes to 1k during peak events. Latency SLO for the first pass is 80ms and end-to-end rerank should be under 300ms ideally.
01:02 Priya Raman: Nice. When you say "first pass" do you mean ANN recall stage then rerank with a cross-encoder?
01:07 Liam O'Connor: Exactly. We do HNSW in FAISS to get 100 candidates, then a CPU cross-encoder to rerank. The cross-encoder is the bottleneck.
01:16 Ethan Li: Ok, good. Couple of high-level choices: you can go Redwood hosted API which is easiest for quick iteration, Redwood Dedicated for reserved GPU capacity and predictable latency, or Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) if you need network isolation and KMS/HSM integration. Any regulatory or data residency needs?
01:31 Mark Tan: Not strict residency, but we need audit logs and KMS support. SOC2 is a must.
01:36 Ethan Li: Understood. We have SOC2, support SAML SSO, RBAC, and KMS options for key control in Private deployments. For Hosted we support customer-managed KMS via BYOK in some regions — Priya can confirm specifics.
01:48 Priya Raman: For hosted, you can bring keys in certain regions, yes. For Private you get full control and HSM options. Audit logs are available across Dedicated and Private; Hosted has audit logs but retention tiers vary.
02:02 Sofia Hernandez: Great. On the embeddings side, we're also debating dimensionality: current 768 from our BERT model, but we considered switching to 1536 dims from newer encoders for better recall. Curious about tradeoffs on storage and throughput on Redwood.
02:18 Priya Raman: Right, dims matter. Higher dimensionality increases memory + index size linearly and can affect ANN speed. For HNSW-type indexes, recall improves with dims but latency/cost go up. You can also compress via product quantization or use lower-dim models — e.g., 768 is often sweet spot, 1536 gives quality gains but double the memory. Redwood supports quantized embeddings on inference at the runtime level and recommendations for quantization profiles in Redwood Optimize.
02:42 Liam O'Connor: Do you have any benchmarks for 768 vs 1536 on throughput?
02:46 Priya Raman: We have internal benchmarks — ballpark: on Dedicated n1-standard GPU pools, vector throughput for ANN lookups is roughly inversely proportional to dim size; so 1536 will be about 40-60% slower depending on index config. We'll include specific numbers in the benchmark plan. Also hybrid search (semantic + keyword filtering) can reduce candidate counts and keep latency down.
03:12 Mark Tan: Hybrid search — we do a lot of keyword filters on metadata (source, recency). Would Redwood handle that natively or do we keep Postgres for filters + vector DB for semantics?
03:22 Ethan Li: Two common patterns: 1) keep metadata in your DB and apply filters before querying vector index, or 2) use vector DBs that support metadata filtering (we integrate with Milvus, Pinecone, Weaviate, and also support calling FAISS indexes). Redwood can orchestrate either — we can route requests to a vector DB with pre-filtering via query filters, or do a filtered fetch from Postgres then pass candidate vectors to the ANN stage. For lowest latency, colocating metadata with the index is usually better.
03:47 Sofia Hernandez: We're leaning to Pinecone today but we've seen cost creep. How does Redwood integrate with Pinecone vs hosting our own Milvus/FAISS?
03:55 Priya Raman: Redwood can integrate with hosted Pinecone as an index backend; that is often simplest but you still pay Pinecone. If you pick Dedicated, you can run your own Milvus or FAISS on the Dedicated pool — that reduces external network hops and gives predictable throughput. For Private, you bring your own index and we can orchestrate local calls.
04:15 Liam O'Connor: How about reranking model placement — do you recommend running the cross-encoder on the same GPU pool as the ANN?
04:22 Priya Raman: Good question. For throughput and latency, colocating rerank on GPU is ideal. Our Dedicated offering lets you run both ANN (on CPU/GPU depending on engine) and cross-encoder rerank on the GPU nodes; runtime supports batching and KV cache for autoregressive models but for cross-encoders it's usually a synchronous call per candidate set. We have batching strategies to amortize costs if you have high QPS.
04:47 Mark Tan: Any tooling to estimate cost tradeoffs?
04:50 Ethan Li: Redwood Optimize provides suggestions for batching, quantization, and model footprints per workload. We'll send a cost simulation for your 200-1k QPS pattern.
04:58 Sofia Hernandez: For the trial, we'd like to run a benchmark with our 100k sample vectors, 1k QPS synthetic, hybrid search, and a rerank with top-100 candidates. Is that feasible?
05:08 Priya Raman: Yes. For the trial we'll propose two tracks: hosted quick-run (limited quota) and a dedicated trial node to mirror your production capacity. For a top-100 rerank at 1k QPS you'll need careful batching and possibly a smaller candidate set via metadata filters to meet the 300ms E2E. We'll draft a benchmark config.
05:30 Liam O'Connor: What about embedding generation? We'll likely generate embeddings offline for the catalog, but for new incoming docs we need online embedding at ~200 QPS. Does Redwood host the embedding model or do we call our own?
05:41 Ethan Li: Both. Hosted Redwood API can return embeddings from curated models; you can also bring your own model or host embeddings on Private. For throughput, we support batching on the inference path and have streaming responses for text generation. For embeddings we optimize kernel selection based on sequence length and model arch.
06:00 Mark Tan: Security question — we need SSO, RBAC, audit logs, and KMS. Also, for Private we need HSM. Are these all available?
06:09 Priya Raman: Yes — SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning, RBAC, audit logs, and KMS integration are supported. HSM options are available for Private deployments. We'll attach the security pack with SOC2 and encryption details.
06:22 Sofia Hernandez: Any gotchas on network topology for Private? We have a VPC with strict egress rules.
06:28 Priya Raman: Private plane requires peered VPCs or direct connect; egress rules need to allow control-plane endpoints and endpoint IPs. We'll share a network runbook.
06:36 Ethan Li: Pricing — high level: hosted is usage-based (per-embedding and per-token/rerank unit), dedicated is fixed monthly + usage adjustments, private is enterprise license + support. We'll send ballpark numbers.
06:48 Liam O'Connor: For upfront evaluation we probably prefer hosted to move fast but will likely shift to dedicated if latency/predictability matters.
06:54 Priya Raman: Makes sense. Also note fallback strategies: if dedicated nodes are saturated, our routing can fall back to hosted equivalents or smaller quantized models to keep latency stable.
07:07 Mark Tan: Good. A couple of nitty-gritty things: 1) can Redwood handle mixed-dimensionality corpora? We have legacy 128-d vectors for some features. 2) Do you support cosine and inner product configs?
07:17 Priya Raman: Yes to both. We support per-index distance settings and mixing dims is possible but we recommend normalizing to a consistent space; heterogeneous dims complicate ANN configs. We can also index multiple collections and do multi-index queries and merge results client-side or in the query planner.
07:35 Sofia Hernandez: Logging and observability — we need token-level cost breakdowns and per-route latency traces.
07:41 Ethan Li: Redwood Console provides per-route and per-model dashboards, token-level cost breakdowns, and tracing hooks you can attach to your APM. We'll show screenshots in the follow-up.
07:52 Liam O'Connor: Anything else we should know about model quantization? We saw artifacts when quantizing our reranker a while back. Does Redwood do quality monitoring?
07:59 Priya Raman: Yes, Redwood Optimize can recommend quant profiles and we support quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to eval sets and prompt sets. For cross-encoders, quantization can be trickier — we'll recommend model/precision combos and run an eval.
08:15 Ethan Li: Alright let's summarize next actions. Ethan to send pricing + security pack. Priya to propose benchmark config and run the test. Liam to share sample vectors and baseline numbers. Any other questions?
08:28 Mark Tan: One ask: can you include a quick note on expected index memory for 100k vectors at 768 vs 1536 dims? Even rough numbers help.
08:36 Priya Raman: We'll include that in the benchmark doc — rough estimate: uncompressed float32 ~ 100k * 768 * 4 bytes = ~307MB; for 1536 it's ~614MB. Index overhead for HNSW can add 30-80% depending on efConstruction. We'll put numbers.
08:56 Sofia Hernandez: Perfect. Thanks.
09:00 Ethan Li: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and schedule the benchmark.
09:04 Liam O'Connor: Thanks, bye.

Notes: Transcript has occasional mis-heard acronyms, e.g., "K V cache" instead of KV cache, and speaker attributions ~mostly accurate. References: security pack link [redwood.com/security-pack], benchmark template [link to shared sheet], pricing deck [link to slide].
